pr_body:
The behavior of this API is to return the same value as
`new Win32Exception(error).Message`, while avoiding the
instantiation of an exception.

Fixes #67872

/cc @danmoseley @dotnet/interop-contrib

issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: Expose method to get system message for system error code
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/interop-contrib See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation This optionally (and typically) retrieves the last system error (with `Marshal.GetLastPinvokeError()`) and the matching system error string (internally using `strerror` or `FormatMessage`) for you: ```c# throw new Win32Exception(); ``` (Separate discussion of the unfortunate naming we have inherited for Win32Exception is [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/26227#issuecomment-747842770).) (Also note that `Marshal.GetLastPinvokeError()` == `Marshal.GetLastWin32Error()` and is distinct to `Marshal.GetLastSystemError()` only in that the latter is oblivious to calls to `Marshal.SetLastPInvokeError()` == `Marshal.SetLastWin32Error`) This is convenient if that's exactly what you want, but has these limitations 1. It's not discoverable, you just have to know. 2. It's easy to accidentally reset the error, eg., ```c# // some pinvoke // some other code potentially resetting the last error by calling into the system directly or indirectly throw new Win32Exception(); // uses the last error code, when perhaps you expected a generic message ``` correct way: ```c# // some pinvoke int errorCode = Marshal.GetLastWin32Error(); // some other code throw new Win32Exception(errorCode); ``` 3. Sometimes you just want the message, you don't want an exception. For example, you want to write to the system log, or do some tracing, like [this](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2ef6ac1c731ce690797847135f040ef5abb29d67/src/libraries/System.ServiceProcess.ServiceController/src/System/ServiceProcess/ServiceBase.cs#L904-L905)), In this case getting the message is clumsy: ```c# string errorMessage = new Win32Exception().Message; ``` or if you want it from the error code: ```c# string errorMessage = new Win32Exception(errorCode).Message; ``` 4. If you want to throw a partially custom message, you have to be even more clumsy, and it's easy to accidentally overwrite the last error. This is not robust because some string formatting machinery runs and potentially resets the last error before Win32Exception internally calls `Marshal.GetLastPinvokeError()`: ```c# throw new Win32Exception($"Could not open SCM. {new Win32Exception().Message}"); ``` This is not robust either because Win32Exception still calls `Marshal.GetLastPinvokeError()` to set its `NativeErrorCode`. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/67827 is an example where this was wrong. ```c# string errorMessage = new Win32Exception().Message; throw new Win32Exception($"Could not delete service '{ServiceName}'. {errorMessage}"); ``` One must write this to be robust ([example in our code](https://github.com/danmoseley/runtime/blob/a431bbc76dd80cb6f960725547ad3ccb5c9cf679/src/libraries/System.Drawing.Common/src/misc/DbgUtil.cs#L57-L59)) ```c# int errorCode = Marshal.GetLastWin32Error(); string errorMessage = new Win32Exception(errorCode).Message; throw new Win32Exception(errorCode, $"Could not delete service '{ServiceName}'. {errorMessage}"); ``` It's unfortunate that Win32Exception calls `Marshal.GetLastPinvokeError()` at all but that can't change now. We can at least help address 1, 3 and 4. ### API Proposal ```C# namespace System.Runtime.InteropServices { public class Marshal { public static int GetLastPInvokeError(); // existing public static string GetMessageforPinvokeError(int error); // Win32Exception parameter name is `error`, although its property is `NativeErrorCode` } } ``` ### API Usage ```C# int errorCode = Marshal.GetLastPinvokeError(); // error is captured here string errorMessage = Marshal.GetMessageforPinvokeError(errorCode); throw new Win32Exception(errorCode, $"Could not delete service '{ServiceName}'. {errorMessage}"); ``` or ```C# int errorCode = Marshal.GetLastPinvokeError(); // error is captured here throw new Win32Exception(errorCode, $"Could not delete service '{ServiceName}'. {Marshal.GetMessageforPinvokeError(errorCode)}"); ``` ### Alternative Designs It would be nice to add overloads to Win32Exception, that eg., take a message to prepend. However, that may not be a common enough requirement, and would be ambiguous with existing string overload. It would probably have to be a static factory method. You'd still need the Marshal method, in case you don't want the exception object. ### Risks _No response_

review_comments:
I wouldn't say it represents the canonical system exception, especially now that you don't need it to get this message.

It's actually not thrown in many places outside of Windows. Essentially Process and Networking, and many of those could throw an existing derived type, then we could squint and pretend it doesn't exist except on Windows.
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/26227#issuecomment-747842770

It doesn't matter of course, just taking exception to the comment..

This test probably isn't enough as it's just testing one method calls the other. The messages should be super stable, so it should be possible to just verify that the message is the expected even if we only test the message for one error code on each platform.

> This test probably isn't enough as it's just testing one method calls the other. 

That isn't what this test is testing. It is verifying our long-standing pattern continues to work and people can use this new API and get the same semantics.

> The messages should be super stable, so it should be possible to just verify that the message is the expected even if we only test the message for one error code on each platform.

I'm not sure how that is possible without hardcoding OS level error messages, which can change. Open to prior art that shows how this is done in libraries.
I don't actually see any existing test of Win32Exception verifying that it uses FormatMessage or equivalent. So such a test can be here.

> so it should be possible to just verify that the message is the expected even if we only test the message for one error code on each platform.

We've generally avoided doing so not only because we don't control them but also because they're localized.

The ideal test would call FormatMessage/strerror and compare the result. As you point out, this hole predates your change, so you need not fix it today. It would just become a hole in Marshal tests rather than Win32Exception tests..
A minimal test would probably verify that the string was not empty, and perhaps that the strings for two codes were not the same.
I don't disbelieve you, but you suspect there are systems on which strerror(EACESS) == strerror(EEXIST) and they are not null?
